purpose: Investigate the original XML default-aggregate RSS increase without replacing the original measurements.
outcome: No production-source optimization applied. Additional first-marshal reflection is measurable but small; available evidence does not attribute the larger RSS difference to that allocation.

source_inventory.selection: regular-file SHA256 and directory/symlink metadata, excluding .git directories

repeat_experiment.method: 20 fresh-process paired default analyze all invocations, alternating baseline/candidate then candidate/baseline; JSON/source=directory/workers=8/tree-size=1000000. Same existing 128-file XML corpus. No instrumentation in these timing/RSS runs.

limitations: Warm caches and same host, without CPU/memory isolation; uncontrolled desktop activity remained.
Only 20 observations per lane: upper sample quantiles are descriptive, not reliable population-tail estimates.
The candidate 112.5625 MiB maximum is retained, not discarded as an outlier.
The additional experiment supplements the original 10-repetition result; it does not establish memory equivalence or erase the original 12.06 percent increase.
No throughput claim is made for reading all 2 GiB; profiling reads selected bounded prefixes.

allocation_instrumentation.method: Fresh optimized Go binaries with symbols retained and only main replaced by the documented temporary overlay. runtime.MemProfileRate=1 after package initialization; ReadMemStats immediately before/after operation, followed by forced GC and allocation/heap profiles. Three fresh processes per version/mode.
allocation_instrumentation.cold_empty_report_definition: First json.Marshal(&profile.Report{}) with every optional module nil. Report bytes match between variants.
limits: Profiling startup and forced GC perturb execution. These captures attribute allocated bytes, not production latency or peak RSS.
Global package initialization occurs before MemProfileRate changes; global allocations are not uniformly sampled at one-byte rate.
The root profiling main uses context.Background and bypasses production signal-handler setup equally for both versions.
Concurrent regexp caches and GC produce run-to-run allocation variation; three captures do not prove allocation equivalence.
The ranking is one candidate CLI attribution capture; it is not a repository-wide cost model.

hypothesis_ledger.hypothesis: New optional report types cause eager JSON encoder construction even when modules are absent.
That new encoder allocation explains the original approximately 8 MiB RSS median increase.
hypothesis_ledger.evidence: Approximately 81 KB extra isolated first-marshal allocation versus approximately 340 MB total CLI allocations; encoder contribution is around 0.13 percent of one candidate capture. No causal GC/RSS reduction was demonstrated.

hypothesis_ledger.hypothesis: New functionality causes a material increase in total allocations for default XML analysis.
hypothesis_ledger.evidence: Three instrumented CLI captures overlap: baseline338442128..354774648 allocated bytes; candidate341814392..348548104 allocated bytes. Both have19..22 GC cycles.

hypothesis_ledger.hypothesis: GC/scheduling and peak-RSS variability contribute to the observed difference.
hypothesis_ledger.evidence: 20-pair repeat has broad RSS ranges, median increase about 2.1 percent rather than original 12.06 percent, and a retained 112.5625 MiB candidate maximum.

recommendation: Do not add lazy MarshalJSON hooks for this release on this evidence. The small eager reflection cost can be considered separately with serialization API parity checks. Keep the original measured RSS increase and limitations visible.

steps: Use the pinned 0.5 release and the candidate identified by build-identity.json for the uninstrumented 20 alternating paired invocations; preserve every RSS sample and exact stdout/stderr/exits.

For allocation attribution, create an ignored Go overlay mapping main.go to instrumentation_main_go. For the reference profile also overlay each changed production Go or embedded *.schema.json file with its v0.5.0 content and map newly added production Go files to deletion. Keep go.mod/go.sum at the reference revision if changed.
Build each profiling executable with CGO_ENABLED=0, go build -overlay=<overlay.json> -trimpath -buildvcs=false -ldflags=-X dircue/internal/cli.Version=0.5.0. Do not add -s/-w; retain symbols.

Set DIRCUE_PROFILE_DIR to a fresh output directory. Set DIRCUE_PROFILE_KIND=empty for first-marshal attribution or cli for analyze all --json --source directory --workers 8 --tree-size 1000000 <XML corpus>. Repeat each mode/version 3 times in fresh processes.
Read stats.json and use go tool pprof -top -sample_index=alloc_space on allocs.pprof; focus=encoding/json isolates encoder construction. No inspected code is executed.
